_note: Run: <torch-venv>/bin/python bin/mutate.py --spec mutations/var-backbone.json --python <torch-venv>/bin/python (an interpreter with torch, so the backbone builds and loads in-process; use an absolute path for --python). This is the A3:var wiring (docs/STEP3_PORTING_PLAN.md): VAR reused as a frozen spatial-backbone kind for the ARSSL harness. VAR's probed representation is measured, not named -- the VQVAE tokeniser's encoder output, global-average-pooled (evaluate_linear_var.encode), not the VAR transformer and not encoder.pt. The VQGAN encoder is fully convolutional (stride 16), so the map needs no token reshape; the provider returns vae.encoder(x) directly and infers the tokeniser arch (ch, Cvae, V) from the checkpoint (the iGPT pattern). The shared discovery/dispatch/KINDS guards are already proven in mutations/mae-backbone.json. These mutations prove the provider's own guards are not vacuous: the encoder output (not the quantised map one step further on) is the read (pooling it reproduces VAR's own probe feature), a checkpoint that is not this tokeniser -- an inference weight it infers arch from, a tokeniser weight, or an alien key -- is refused rather than half-loaded, and the backbone stays frozen in eval (its train() override). NOTE: the provider's own `requires_grad = False` loop is deliberately NOT a mutation target -- it is an equivalent mutant. Measured: the shared downstream/spatial_backbones.build_frozen_backbone re-freezes every returned model's parameters (`for p in model.parameters(): p.requires_grad = False`, lines 197-198) after the provider returns, so flipping the provider's own loop to True cannot change the observable frozen state through the only path the tests (and production) reach it. The aim/igpt specs omit it for the same reason; the requires_grad guard belongs to the shared layer, not per provider.

targets.label: the quantised map (one conv further on) is read instead of the encoder output, so the feature is not VAR's own probe feature
a checkpoint carrying keys this VQVAE does not have is half-loaded, not refused
a checkpoint missing a tokeniser weight is silently accepted
the architecture is inferred from a checkpoint that has no encoder input convolution, so a non-tokeniser is built against a guessed shape instead of being refused
the backbone leaves eval when train() is called
the build leaves the submodule root on sys.path, so a later `from models import ...` resolves to VAR's models (the cross-method import bug)
the build leaves the modules it newly imported (VAR's models) bound under the shared keys, not deleting them
the build does not put back a shared module it overwrote (a method's own `models` bound before the build stays replaced by VAR's)
the build leaves the global torch RNG advanced, so a later unseeded draw is shifted (tipping an RNG-fragile finite assertion into NaN)
the build does not put back torch's default init on a class the upstream replaced it on (nn.Linear stays a no-op), so every module a later method builds keeps uninitialised torch.empty memory (NaN)
the build does not remove an override the upstream added to a class that had none of its own (nn.Conv2d keeps the no-op), so a later module built from it is uninitialised

_result.measured_on: 2026-09-01 (re-measured after the hermetic-build guards were extended to torch's default parameter init: VAR's upstream build_vae_var setattr's nn.<cls>.reset_parameters to a no-op over eight classes globally and permanently, so every module a later method builds keeps uninitialised torch.empty memory -- the real cause of the 53 cross-method not-finite / not-round-tripping failures in the in-process suite. The provider now snapshots and restores each nn class's own reset_parameters alongside sys.path, sys.modules and the torch RNG, so building the tokeniser leaves no observable global side effect in the shared process)
_result.measured_with: an interpreter with torch (.venvs/05_jigsaw_puzzle), which builds and loads the VAR VQVAE backbone in-process; the end-to-end ARSSL test is not among the referenced tests, so no timm subprocess is needed to kill these
